tokenizer_check_css_syntax_3.3.3 preprocessing: Tokenizer::at (cssurl.rs:204-213): CR LF, CR, FF -> LF; U+0000 -> U+FFFD; &str has no surrogates. Matches 3.3 'filter code points'.

new_findings.kind: security (asset gate hides a browser-loaded URL; R5/R6/R10-F1 FAIL class: the crate reads the text differently from the browser before classifying; R9 normalised-text rule: the consumer must read the pieces the browser hands to CSS)
new_findings.file_line: handshake-studio-assets/crates/hsk-studio-web/src/assets.rs:641-648 (an animation attribute keeps Kind::Css for `values`; only Kind::Url becomes Kind::UrlValues) and :542 (`Kind::Css => self.css(node, &source, text, &sub)` tokenizes the whole decoded `values` text as ONE CSS text); target resolution animated_kind :575-589.
new_findings.evidence: Browsers split a SMIL values list on every ';' BEFORE parsing each piece as a CSS value: Blink SVGAnimationElement::ParseValues (svg_animation_element.cc:58-80, `StringView(value).Split(';')`, used for kValuesAnimation :698-704); Gecko SMILAnimationFunction.cpp:697 -> SMILParserUtils::ParseValues/ParseValuesGeneric (SMILParserUtils.cpp:524-552, nsCharSeparatedTokenizer on ';') -> SMILValueParser::Parse -> SMILCSSProperty::ValueFromString per piece. A comment, string or bad url opened in one piece therefore ends at the ';' for the browser but swallows the rest of the list for the crate. Payload: `<svg><rect width="9" height="9"><animate attributeName="mask" dur="1s" values="none /*;url(https://evil.example/m.png)"/></rect></svg>`. Browser: pieces `none /*` (valid, trailing comment) and `url(https://evil.example/m.png)` (valid mask image, fetched when the animation reaches it). Crate: css_references("none /*;url(https://evil.example/m.png)") reads ident none, whitespace, then 4.3.2 consumes the comment to EOF -> no reference; no Engines/Gecko reading runs (ASCII, no backslash); collect_assets reports nothing and the port is never asked. Same with fill/stroke/filter/clip-path/marker-*/cursor targets, and with a relative URL (`values="none /*;url(private/m.png)"`): an ungranted relative asset is loaded without the port being consulted. A bad-url decoy (`url(a b;url(evil)`) also hides the later URL behind its remnants. Secondary: `values="url(a;b)"` is reported as "a;b" while the browser parses the piece `url(a` ("a"). No test covers a CSS-target values list: svg_animation_of_href_is_scanned (tests/source_dom_patch.rs:1764-1790) covers href values and fill from/to only; css_url_gate carriers() (tests/css_url_gate.rs:85-93) has no animation carrier; the difftest css-urls carriers (tests/html5ever_differential/harness.rs:161-173) are style + presentation attributes only, and css_reference shares the gate policy, so the class is invisible to every committed check. The DESCRIPTOR row and collect_assets doc claiming 'every URL a browser loads' for 'to, from, by and values' are falsified (V4-07).
new_findings.remediation: For an animation attribute named `values` whose target kind is Kind::Css, split the decoded text on every ';' exactly as the engines do (naive split, no CSS awareness; trim HTML whitespace) and run css_references on each piece with its own offset (span via `sub` when exact, else the whole value), like Kind::UrlValues; keep to/from/by whole. V4-08 tests in css_url_gate (new animation carrier for set/animate to/from/by/values on fill and mask): comment decoy (`none /*;url(evil)`), bad-url decoy (`url(a b;url(evil)`), unterminated-string decoy, escaped name in a later piece (`none /*;\75 rl(evil)`), case/whitespace (`URL( evil )`, attributeName=FILL), `url(a;b)` reports "a" not "a;b", and a relative later piece that reaches the port. Add the animation carrier (split the same way) to the difftest css-urls check and corpus.

new_findings.kind: security (asset gate hides a browser-loaded URL in the SVG-animation CSS carrier; same class)
new_findings.file_line: handshake-studio-assets/crates/hsk-studio-web/src/assets.rs:161-165 (the CSS-attribute list fill|stroke|clip-path|cursor|filter|mask|marker-start|marker-mid|marker-end has no `marker`), reached from animated_kind :584-588 (`attr_kind("", &target)?` -> None for attributeName=marker, so to/from/by/values are not classified at :641-651).
new_findings.evidence: Gecko animates any CSS property in SMILCSSProperty::IsPropertyAnimatable when attributeName names it: SMILCompositor::GetCSSPropertyToAnimate (SMILCompositor.cpp:146-160: nsCSSProps::LookupProperty(attributeName), then IsPropertyAnimatable) and SMILCSSProperty.cpp:150 lists eCSSProperty_marker (the marker shorthand; shorthands are supported, GetBaseValue :43-58). `marker` is not a presentation attribute in Blink (svg_element.cc:319-380) or Gecko (SVGElement.cpp IsNoNamespaceAttrMapped), so only the animation path loads it. Payload: `<svg><path d="M0 0L9 9"><set attributeName="marker" to="url(private/markers.svg#m)"/></path></svg>`: Firefox sets marker-start/mid/end and fetches markers.svg as an external resource document; the crate reports nothing and never asks the port (an ungranted relative asset is loaded). With `to="url(https://evil.example/m.svg#m)"` the external reference is neither reported nor denied. Every other URL-taking property in Gecko's SMIL list (clip-path, cursor, fill, filter, marker-start/mid/end, mask, stroke) is covered. No test covers attributeName=marker.
new_findings.remediation: Treat attributeName `marker` (ASCII case-insensitive, already lower-cased at :580) as a Kind::Css animation target in animated_kind (adding `marker` to the CSS-attribute list is also acceptable: over-reporting is safe). Tests: set/animate attributeName=marker and MARKER with to/from/by/values carrying external, relative, escaped (\75 rl() and comment-decoy values; one assertion that the relative value reaches the port. Update DESCRIPTOR assets.scanned and the collect_assets doc.
